kurz: What complete account data sets from Brazil and Taiwan show about traders' success rate, and where the percentage under every CFD advert comes from.

bloecke.md:
How many traders make money is a question that can be answered. Surveys of active traders are not suitable for this, however, and forum posts even less so. Both sources only capture traders who are still active. The only usable data sets are those that cover a complete population, including accounts that have since been closed. Two such analyses exist, and they independently arrive at the same order of magnitude.

Chague, De-Losso and Giovannetti observed all private individuals who began day trading in the Brazilian equity index futures market between 2013 and 2015. By volume, this market is the third largest in the world. Of the persistent ones who kept going for more than 300 trading days, 97% lost money. The proportion who earned more than the Brazilian minimum wage was 1.1%, and the proportion who earned more than the starting salary of a bank teller was 0.5%. These traders did not pursue day trading on the side, because 300 trading days is more than a full working year in front of the screen.

bloecke.titel: Results of Brazilian day traders with more than 300 trading days
bloecke.unter: Chague/De-Losso/Giovannetti, observation period 2013-2015. The second bar is the arithmetic complement of the first, and the two lower values are subsets of it.

Earned more than a bank employee in their first year

bloecke.md:
## Fifteen years of day trading in Taiwan

Barber, Lee, Liu, Odean and Zhang analysed the complete transaction data of the Taiwan Stock Exchange from 1992 to 2006. The data cover every trade on this venue and are not a sample of the customers of a single broker. The aggregate net performance of all day traders after fees was negative in every single one of the fifteen years. The share of profitable day traders was consistently around 5%. Fewer than 1% earned profits after costs predictably and reliably.

For perception, however, attrition is the most important finding. More than 75% of day traders quit within two years, and traders who have quit no longer write posts. What remains visible is the small group that happens to be winning. Readers of such posts therefore systematically overestimate the success rate. This is a typical case of [[Survivorship bias (Überlebensbias)|survivorship bias]].

The data also show that losses hardly deter people from continuing to trade. Of the day trading volume, 72% came from traders who had previously been unprofitable, and in the last years of the sample it was around 80%. Traders who had made losses with at least 50 trading days of experience continued trading in the following year with a probability of 95.3%. Among the profitable traders, the figure was 96.4%. When it comes to the decision to quit, winners and losers therefore differ by just over one percentage point.

bloecke.md:
## Reasons for the low success rate

Before costs, short-term trading is approximately a zero-sum game in which one party's gain corresponds to another's loss. After costs, the sum across all participants is necessarily negative, because order fees, spread, slippage and, for leveraged products, financing costs are deducted from this sum. The success rate in the studies is therefore the expected consequence of this arithmetic identity and not a chance finding. The only open question is how much the rate shifts as trading frequency and leverage increase, and that can be calculated.

bloecke.formel: Capital after n round turns = Capital × (1 − L × c)^n
bloecke.erklaerung: The illustrative calculation assumes the neutral case, a trading idea that earns exactly nothing before costs. The friction c is incurred on the nominal volume, but the account is measured by its equity. That is why the leverage L appears as a factor in the formula in every single period.
variablen: leverage: nominal volume divided by the equity employed
friction per round turn, relative to the nominal volume: order fee for entry and exit, half the spread on each side, slippage and, where applicable, financing costs
number of complete entries and exits in the year
bloecke.beispiel: With c = 0.10% and n = 250, 77.9% of the capital remains without leverage, 28.6% with leverage of 5 and 0.6% with leverage of 20. This loss arises from friction alone, without a single wrong move.

bloecke.titel: Remaining capital depending on leverage (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.unter: Remaining capital as a percentage, with friction of 0.10% per round turn on the nominal volume and a trading idea with no return before costs. Higher leverage accelerates the decline but does not change its direction.

bloecke.md: Leverage does not change the expected value per euro traded. Per euro of equity, it multiplies gain, loss and costs in the same proportion. If the expected value is zero before costs and negative after costs, this remains the case even with leverage of 30; only the time until the capital is lost becomes shorter. The common justification “with a small account, it isn't worth it any other way” turns the argument on its head. It cites a small account as a reason for more risk, even though a small account calls for less risk.

## Loss rate in CFD advertising

Under every CFD advert in the EU there is a sentence stating a loss rate. Providers do not publish it voluntarily; it has been mandatory since the ESMA measure of 23 March 2018. The supervisor had previously analysed providers' account data. Depending on the provider, 74% to 89% of retail accounts lost money, and average losses per client were between €1,600 and €29,000. In addition to the mandatory disclosure, the measure introduced leverage limits, a mandatory close-out at 50% of the required initial margin and negative balance protection per account. The initially temporary measure was adopted permanently at national level.

The disclosure is therefore the industry's only regularly updated success statistic. It applies to the individual provider, comes from its own books and is not based on a selection of those who report. A figure that does not come from a study can thus be found in the footer of the advertising whose message it contradicts.

bloecke.titel: ESMA leverage limits for retail clients since 2018

bloecke.md: With leverage L, the initial margin is 1/L of the nominal value. The close-out is triggered when half of it has been used up, that is, after a price movement of 50/L% against the position. At 30:1, that is 1.67%; at 5:1, 10%. There are two qualifications. The rule operates at account level across all open positions together, and a buffer of free balance shifts the trigger point accordingly. Price movements of 1.67% on a single day are rare for major currency pairs and become more frequent in times of crisis. Over several weeks, on the other hand, an adverse move often reaches this size.

## The business model of trading education

If only a small proportion of traders earn money over the long term, the fact that so many teach trading needs an explanation. In economic terms, a course fee is a certain, immediately payable income per participant, whereas a trading account is an uncertain income with a negative expected value after costs. Someone who has mastered both would therefore fund their trading with the course fees and not the other way round.

In addition, there are the industry's remuneration structures. Affiliate and introducing broker programmes pay for referred, funded accounts or give the intermediary a share of the trading turnover. Where such a programme exists, the second income stream depends on the student's trading volume and not on their result. This feature of the business model applies regardless of the individual provider and should be known before buying. The Brazilian study is explicitly directed against the providers' promises. The authors present their finding under the phrase “contrary to what course providers claim”.

bloecke.titel: Income streams in the trading course business
bloecke.unter: Two of the three income streams are independent of the participant's trading result. Only the bottom one depends on it, and it is the only one with a negative expected value after costs.

earns on spread, fees, financing, depending on volume

bloecke.md:
Under the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer), Section 20(9) EStG (Income Tax Act) excludes the deduction of income-related expenses (Werbungskosten). The only deduction is the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000 per person, or €2,000 for joint assessment. Seminar fees, charting software, data feeds and trading computers therefore do not reduce the tax. Gains, on the other hand, are taxed at 25% (Section 32d(1) EStG), plus 5.5% solidarity surcharge under Section 4 SolzG 1995 (Solidarity Surcharge Act), so 26.375% in total.

A buyer who pays €2,000 for a course and has used up the allowance elsewhere therefore needs a gross profit of 2,000 / (1 − 0.26375) = €2,716 just to recoup the fee in the first year. Relative to a portfolio of €20,000, that is 13.6% of additional gross return. Only what is earned beyond that is profit.

The figures do not mean that skill does not exist. In the Taiwan data, there is a group with a predictably positive net return, but it comprises fewer than 1% of day traders. According to the 2017 working paper version, this group makes up under 3% of all day traders on an average day and generates 9.81% of day trading volume. In the published version, these detailed figures may differ slightly.

Nor do the figures apply to every form of active trading. What was measured was day trading in two markets and two periods. For US private households without day trading, the return decreases step by step as trading activity increases. The most active fifth achieved 11.4% a year, the market 17.9%. Frequent trading there led to lagging behind the market, but not to ruin.

The figures also say nothing about any single individual. A base rate only indicates the starting probability against which a person would have to present evidence, specifically their own evidence, documented and calculated after costs and taxes.

- The return is calculated on a time-weighted basis and not in euros, because deposits and withdrawals distort any percentage figure derived from the account balance minus deposits.
- Open positions at the price on the reporting date, all fees, financing costs and taxes paid must be included. Course fees and data feeds also belong in the cost calculation, even though they bring no tax benefit.
- The benchmark is a broad index over the same period, likewise after costs and taxes. Without a benchmark, you are only measuring the direction of the market.
- The minimum period is set in advance and not in retrospect, because over a few months every result is noise.
- A quitting threshold is written down in advance. The Taiwan data show that losses barely reduce the probability of continuing to trade. A threshold that is only set while in a loss does not serve its purpose.

mitnehmen: In complete account data sets, a few per cent of day traders make money; of the persistent Brazilian day traders, 97% lost money, and in Taiwan around 5% were profitable and fewer than 1% predictably profitable.
More than 75% of day traders quit within two years, so forums and social media show a selection of those who remain and not a representative sample.

Leverage does not change the sign of the expected value and only accelerates the loss; with friction of 0.10% per round turn and 250 round turns, 77.9% of the capital remains without leverage, and only 0.6% with leverage of 20.
The percentage under CFD advertising goes back to the 2018 ESMA measure; at that time, 74% to 89% of retail accounts lost money.
A course fee is certain income for the provider and not tax-deductible for the buyer (Section 20(9) EStG), whereas any income from what has been learned is uncertain.

begriffe.text: A complete trading transaction consisting of entry and exit. The friction costs of a round turn comprise the order fee for both sides, half the spread on each side and the slippage. They relate to the nominal volume.
Rule from the 2018 ESMA measure. If the account balance falls below 50% of the initial margin required for the open positions, the provider must close the positions.

Limitation of a retail client's loss to the balance of the CFD account concerned. An obligation to make additional payments beyond this balance is excluded. The protection applies per account and not per position.
Bias that arises because those who failed disappear from the statistics. In trading, it has a double effect, because those who quit appear neither in broker analyses nor in forums.

Remuneration model in which an intermediary is paid for referred, funded accounts or with a share of the trading turnover. The intermediary's income depends on the trading volume of the referred client and not on the client's trading result.
